Randomly sample sequences from a FASTA file

Source: R/vtamR_fun.R
random_sample_fasta.Rd

Randomly samples a specified number of sequences from a FASTA file and writes the sampled sequences to an output file. The input file is processed in chunks to avoid loading the entire FASTA file into memory.

Usage

random_sample_fasta(
  fasta,
  outfile,
  n = 1e+06,
  randseed = NULL,
  chunk_lines = 1e+05,
  compress_method = "R",
  pigz_path = NULL,
  num_threads = 0,
  quiet = TRUE,
  fast_count = TRUE,
  total_reads = NULL,
  log_file = NULL
)

Arguments

fasta

Character string giving the path to the input FASTA file. Files ending in .gz are treated as gzip-compressed.

outfile

Character string giving the path to the output FASTA file. A filename ending in .gz produces gzip-compressed output.

n

Integer specifying the number of sequences to sample. Sampling is performed without replacement. Defaults to 1e6.

randseed

Optional integer used to initialize the random number generator with set.seed. Setting this argument makes the sampling reproducible.

chunk_lines

Integer specifying the maximum number of lines read from the input file at a time. Smaller values reduce memory usage but may increase processing time. Larger values may improve performance at the cost of increased memory usage. Defaults to 1e5.

compress_method

Character string specifying the compression method used by fast_copy when the complete input file is copied. Supported values are "R", "pigz", and "gzip". Defaults to "R".

pigz_path

Optional path to the pigz executable. If NULL (default), resolved via getOption("vtamR.pigz_path") or the PATH (see get_path).

num_threads

Integer specifying the number of threads to use when compress_method = "pigz". A value of 0 uses all detected CPU cores. Defaults to 0.

quiet

Logical indicating whether progress messages should be suppressed. Defaults to TRUE.

fast_count

Logical value controlling the counting method. When TRUE on Linux, shell commands are used for faster counting. When FALSE, the chunk-based R implementation is used on all operating systems. This argument is passed to count_reads.

total_reads

Integer or NULL. The total number of sequences in the input file, if already known (e.g. from a pre-computed value or an info file). If NULL (the default), the function will count the sequences in the file itself, which can be slow for large files. Supplying total_reads skips this counting step and uses the given value directly, so it is the caller's responsibility to ensure it is correct.

log_file

Character string specifying the path to the CSV log file. The path is resolved with the following priority:

  1. the log_file argument, if explicitly provided by the user;

  2. the vtamR.log_file option set with options(vtamR.log_file = ...), if set;

  3. "vtamR_log.csv" in the current working directory, used as a last resort if neither of the above is set.

To disable logging entirely, set log_file = NA.

Value

Invisibly returns the number of sequences requested by n. If n is greater than or equal to the total number of sequences, the total number of sequences in the input file is returned instead.

Details

Sampling is performed without replacement, and the selected sequence positions are sorted before extraction. Both compressed (.gz) and uncompressed FASTA files are supported through open_any.

If the requested number of sequences is greater than or equal to the total number of sequences in the input file, no sampling is performed and the entire input file is copied to the output using fast_copy.

The function first counts the total number of sequences in the input FASTA file using count_reads. It then randomly selects n sequence positions using sample.int.

The FASTA file is subsequently read in chunks of chunk_lines lines. Sequence boundaries are tracked across chunks so that sequences split between two chunks are handled correctly. Only selected sequences are written to the output file.

Because the selected sequence indices are stored in memory, the memory required for sampling is primarily determined by the number of sequences in the input file and the requested sample size, rather than by the total size of the FASTA sequence data.

If randseed is provided, it is passed to set.seed before sampling, allowing the same subset of sequences to be reproduced.

See also

count_reads, fast_copy, open_any, sample.int

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Randomly sample 10,000 sequences
random_sample_fasta("sequences.fasta",
                    "sample.fasta",
                    n = 10000)

# Sample from a gzip-compressed FASTA file
random_sample_fasta("sequences.fasta.gz",
                    "sample.fasta.gz",
                    n = 10000)

# Use a fixed seed for reproducible sampling
random_sample_fasta("sequences.fasta",
                    "sample.fasta",
                    n = 10000,
                    randseed = 123)

# Use pigz for compression when copying a file that has less than n sequences
random_sample_fasta("sequences.fasta",
                    "sample.fasta.gz",
                    n = 10000,
                    compress_method = "pigz",
                    num_threads = 4)
} # }
